NISHIT A BHALODI(9597) for the Applicant(s) No. 1,2,3,4,5,6  MASUMI V NANAVATY(9321) for the Respondent(s) No. 3  MR VIBHUTI NANAVATI(513) for the Respondent(s) No. 3  RULE SERVED for the Respondent(s) No. 1,2  ================================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MR. JUSTICE DEVAN M. DESAI  Date : 11/03/2025
ORAL ORDER 1.
This application is filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act, 1963 for condonation of delay of 1273 days caused in preferring the First Appeal.

2. Heard learned advocate Mr.Nishit Bhalodi for the applicants and learned advocate Mr. Vibhuti Nanavati for respondent No.3.
3.
Learned advocate for the applicants has submitted that the applicant has good case on merits as well as on law.
It is further submitted that applicant had to collect NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/128/2025 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2025 undefined necessary papers and arrange Court fees and other expenses.
It is further submitted that delay may be condoned as there is no intentional delay on the part of the applicants.

sentences.text: It is further submitted that the present applicants are unaware of the provisions of law, which could permit him to file appeal, which is a statutory right.
He has submitted that the applicants have filed an affidavit dated 28.02.2025, which is placed on record.

From the said affidavit, the claimants has undertaken to waive the interest upon the enhanced compensation, if any, for the delay period,
if appellants succeeds in First Appeal.
It is further submitted that claimants have further undertaken that they will not raise ground of enhancement in consortium amount, loss to estate and funeral expenses at the time of final hearing.

It is further submitted that in view of the settled principles of law in the decision of NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/128/2025 ORDER DATED: 11/03/2025 undefined Hon'ble Apex Court in case of K. Subbarayadu and others Vs.

The Special Deputy Collector (Land Acquisition) reported in 2017(12) SCC 840 and would submit that considering the law laid down in aforementioned case, the applicants are not claiming their right for the interest upon the enhanced compensation, if any, for the delay period, if appellants succeeds in First Appeal.

4. Per contra, learned advocate for the respondent No.3 has objected and submitted that the reasons assigned in the application does not inspire any confidence to condone the delay and therefore,
application may be dismissed by this Court.

5. Considering the submissions canvassed by the learned advocates for the respective parties and contentions raised in the application, it is needless to observe that in catena of decisions, the view taken by the Hon'ble Supreme Court NEUTRAL CITATION C/CA/128/2025 ORDER DATED:
11/03/2025 undefined is, while deciding an application for condonation of delay, the liberal and justice orientated approach needs to be adopted so that the substantive rights of the parties are not defeated only on the ground of delay.
To meet with the equity, delay can be condoned.
There is no intentional delay on the part of the applicant.
The delay has sufficiently been explained.
Hence, the delay is condoned subject to condition that the claimant/s shall not claim interest upon enhanced compensation, if any, for the period of delay, if succeeds the appeal.
6. With these observations and directions and considering the aforesaid affidavit dated 28.02.2025 filed by the claimants, the present Civil Application stands allowed.
Rule is made absolute to the aforesaid extent.
